question: A 72-year-old male visits his gastroenterologist for a check-up one year following resection of a 2-cm malignant lesion in his sigmoid colon. Serum levels of which of the following can be used in this patient to test for cancer recurrence?

enhanced_information: In the context of a 72-year-old male with a history of sigmoid colon cancer, monitoring for cancer recurrence is crucial following surgical resection. The standard serum tumor marker used for this purpose is Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), which is specifically associated with colorectal cancer. Elevated levels of CEA can indicate possible recurrence of the disease. Other markers such as Alpha-fetoprotein, CA-125, and CA-19-9 are not typically used for monitoring colorectal cancer recurrence. Therefore, the most relevant and consensus-supported marker for this patient is Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA).
